notes: Expected retrieval numbers for the synthetic CI fixture (account 9001,
scripts/seed_eval_fixture.py) scored against evals/golden/ci_fixture.yaml.
The eval job fails if the app's retrieval precision@5 or recall@10, or
either number for a list under `candidates`, drops more than `tolerance`
below these values. Rising numbers never fail the gate. `retrieval` is
the hybrid search the app runs (app/retrieval/search.py); `candidates`
scores what the resume builder hands the model (app/evals/candidates.py):
skills by name, projects by repository, over the 8 skill_evidence pairs.
These are a canary for retrieval breaking, not a quality measurement:
the data behind them is invented. See the header of ci_fixture.yaml.
Last re-recorded when search moved from one dense query to hybrid search
(per-skill sub-queries fused with the full query by reciprocal rank) and
precision@k began dividing by k. On this fixture precision@5 rose from
0.585 to 0.615 and recall@10 fell from 0.962 to 0.923, one document in
one pair; on the 26 real-text pairs (evals/real/) precision@5 rose from
0.515 to 0.823. Candidate skills precision@5 moved from 0.575 to 0.600
only because of the denominator change.
Skill sub-queries later dropped their dense run (keyword only), after
held-out LinkedIn postings showed the dense runs adding noise for skills
an account lacks. These numbers did not move; the held-out result is in
evals/results/public-fresh-20261009T013435Z.md.
To update deliberately, when a change legitimately moves the numbers:
run `make eval-fixture`, confirm the new numbers are what the change
should have produced, copy them into `retrieval` or `candidates` below, and
say in the commit message which change moved them and why the new value is right.
Never update this file to make a red build go green without that.
tolerance_reasoning: Absolute, not relative, and applied to each metric separately.
Measured rather than guessed. Seeding and scoring were repeated three
times on one machine; once more after deleting the database and the
Qdrant collections so every vector was recomputed from the model; and
once on a GitHub Actions runner, a different operating system, CPU and
Python build. All five runs returned the same floats, bit for bit, to
the last digit of a double. Against a Qdrant server and against
qdrant-client's local mode the ranked ids and their order matched too;
only the cosine scores differed, in the sixth decimal place, which is
far too small to reorder anything here.
So the tolerance is not absorbing observed noise, because there is
none. It is set below the smallest move either metric can make: with
13 pairs, one document changing places in one pair's top-k moves
precision@5 by 0.2/13 = 0.0154 and recall@10 by at least 1/4 relevant
ids /13 = 0.0192. At 0.01 the gate therefore fails on any single
document that stops being retrieved, and is non-zero only so that it
tests ranking rather than float equality.
CI installs from constraints.txt, so a torch or sentence-transformers
release cannot change these vectors unless that file changes. When
`make constraints` re-pins it, run the eval gate before committing: a
moved number there is the dependency upgrade, not the code.
